quotes.text: Learn how to accept the MB WAY payment method.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: MB WAY supports international phone numbers, but the majority of customers use a Portuguese phone number starting with +351.
If you don’t want to use dynamic payment methods, follow the steps below to manually configure the payment methods in your Checkout integration.
The customer receives a notification about the payment request, and authorizes or declines the request in their MB WAY app.
By default, Stripe.js polls for updates to the PaymentIntent.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mb-way/accept-a-payment, new raw lines 5-15 identify the MB WAY acceptance guide and give distinct Checkout, Elements and Direct API navigation. The May 7 capture supplies the actual behavior. Customers initiate with a phone number, which can be international, and approve or decline in the MB WAY app. Checkout uses a Session in payment mode with all line item Prices in EUR. The guide offers dynamic method selection and specifies adding mb_way for manual configuration. Elements and Direct API both start from a server-created EUR PaymentIntent with mb_way and a client secret. The dated web Payment Element example uses the beta flag and stripe.confirmPayment. Direct API uses browser-side stripe.confirmMbWayPayment with the phone in billing details. Its default polling follows the Intent to succeeded or a failure return to requires_payment_method. Use the server-side payment success event or the Checkout fulfillment route for business actions (old raw lines 8-12, old raw lines 14-51, old raw lines 106-125, old raw lines 149-167, old raw lines 248-267, old raw lines 390-432, old raw lines 567-585, old raw lines 654-720). source-stripe-mb-way-accept-payment.md lines 13–34 capture the headline routes and cases but omit dynamic Checkout, the app authorization and outcome boundaries, and the explicit sandbox qualifier.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mb-way/accept-a-payment, new raw lines 5-15 replace the inline guide with three links and establish a presentation and navigation change. The May 7 implementation remains dated, including EUR and payment-mode requirements for Checkout, the separate browser confirmation methods, the web Payment Element with PaymentIntents beta examples, and automatic versus manual Direct API polling. Add reciprocal warnings in source-stripe-mb-way-accept-payment.md and the Wallets concept’s MB WAY entry. The beta flag belongs to the May web Payment Element with PaymentIntents examples, and the distinct overview links a Checkout Sessions quickstart without establishing the current flag requirement. 'Any other' immediate success and the five named numbers are May sandbox simulations. Immediate outcome notification follows customer authorization or failure, and the Direct API promise may return a failure state. A Checkout return or client callback does not prove payment, settlement or fulfillment. Keep the existing dated raw and use the November variant links for navigation (old raw lines 8-12, old raw lines 24-51, old raw lines 114-125, old raw lines 248-267, old raw lines 317-361, old raw lines 654-720).
